fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, sends word to Hoham, Piram, Japhia and Debir. His message says, “Come up and help me. We will attack Gibeon…” (Joshua 10:4). He's alarmed, so he does what you do when the group chat is the only plan you've got. Four messages go out, and he's not doing this one alone.

I get it, alarmed people sometimes head for the exits. But the text never says he moves his people out of Jerusalem. It says he sends word to four kings and asks them to come up and help him attack Gibeon (Joshua 10:3-4). Then the five kings join forces, advance with all their armies and camp before Gibeon (Joshua 10:5). Adoni-zedek isn't running from this problem, he's recruiting for it.

Chains would be a neat way to stop an army, but I don't see any in this story. Verse 10 says the LORD threw them into confusion before Israel (Joshua 10:10). No rope, no locks, just an army that suddenly can't get its act together. I've had mornings like that with a bowl of dough and no recipe, but never with a whole army!
